messages.content: Quick Kansas City check: United emailed that the outbound is now 18 minutes later, landing at 1:49 p.m. Wednesday. Host pickup is Thursday at 8:35 outside the Crossroads hotel. Friday return still leaves 3:05. Do I need to move earlier?

I would leave it unchanged. With carry-on only, landing at 1:49 still gets you to Crossroads around 2:45-3:10 by rideshare, so check-in and a simple dinner are still fine. Thursday pickup has plenty of margin.
Good. Hotel says check-in is 3:00 and they will hold a bag Friday. Should I send any room notes now?

Yes: ask them to confirm breakfast hours, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, Wi-Fi, your reserved room type, and Friday bag storage after checkout. Also save the cancellation deadline and itemized total.
So no re-shopping unless something else changes?
Correct. Keep the United flight and Crossroads hotel. Re-shop only if the outbound slips another 30-45 minutes or the host pickup moves materially earlier.

messages.content: Kansas City is wrapped. Can we start Minneapolis? April 22-24 from Chicago for the board/grantee convening. Reception Wednesday at 6, Thursday downtown sessions, Friday committee wrap-up expected to end around noon. Please compare flight + hotel pairings, no rental car if practical. I care about total estimate, arrival/return timing, breakfast, in-room coffee/fridge, and easy dinner options.
Sure. A few inputs before I price the pairings: ORD only or is Midway acceptable, any airline to favor if fares are close, and do you have the event hotel or block rate?

ORD is easier. Midway is okay only if it saves real money. United is fine if it is comparable, but timing matters more. The block hotel is the Hilton Minneapolis at $219 before tax, cutoff next week. Reception is either there or next door.

Got it. I will keep Friday departures after lunch and avoid routings that add delay risk for such a short trip. Are you checking a bag, and would you take the Blue Line from MSP if it is straightforward?
Carry-on only. Light rail is fine on the way in if it is direct and daylight. For the return I may use a rideshare so I am not dragging a bag after the committee meeting.

Here is a first-pass comparison using main-cabin nonstop fares and refundable-looking hotel rates; taxes and rideshares are estimates, so I would verify before purchase. Pairing | Flights | Hotel | Est. total | Why it works | Trade-off. A Event-hotel/simple | United ORD-MSP about 12:55-2:25 Wed; MSP-ORD about 2:45-4:15 Fri, about $306 | Hilton block, 2 nights about $504 after tax | about $845 with light rail in and rideshare back | zero commute to sessions, on-site restaurant, easy reception | no included hotel breakfast shown; mini-fridge should be verified. B Breakfast/value | Same United flights | Residence Inn at The Depot/riverfront, about $179 pre-tax, $412 after tax | about $805-$820 with 2 short local rideshares | breakfast included, kitchen-style room with coffee/fridge, Mill District dinner nearby | 7-10 minute ride or 15-18 minute walk to Hilton. C Lowest fare | Southwest from MDW, arrive early afternoon; return around 2:15 Fri, about $250-$270 | Residence Inn or similar breakfast hotel | about $750-$780 | cheaper airfare and breakfast | less convenient Chicago airport for you and a slightly tighter Friday return.
That is helpful. I would rather not use a basic fare, and I would not switch to Midway for only $40.

Then I would drop the Southwest pairing unless it is dramatically cheaper at booking. The useful comparison is really Hilton block plus an ORD nonstop versus a riverfront breakfast-included hotel plus short rideshares.
Can you separate the hotels from the airline, using the United timing as the flight assumption?

Yes. With the United fare held at about $306: Hotel | 2-night lodging after tax | Meeting access | Breakfast/room basics | Dinner | Total with flight + transfers. Hilton Minneapolis block | about $504 | in the building or next door | breakfast not listed; coffee maker likely; mini-fridge or request line needs confirmation | on-site restaurant/bar plus Nicollet options | about $845. Residence Inn at The Depot | about $412 | 7-10 min ride, 15-18 min walk in decent weather | breakfast included; coffee maker and fridge/kitchen setup listed | Mill District and hotel-adjacent casual choices | about $805-$820. Hampton/Convention Center fallback | about $380-$395 if refundable at $165-$172 | 8-12 min walk or short ride | breakfast included; coffee and mini-fridge generally listed | no strong on-site dinner, but close to downtown restaurants | about $775-$800.
If Thursday starts at 8:00 inside the Hilton, does the lower hotel still make sense?

It would still be defensible on cost, but the savings shrink once you add at least one early rideshare. If the 8:00 start is inside the Hilton, I would give the block hotel the edge because it removes the one unpredictable local move of the trip.
And if the first thing Thursday is 9:00 at the arts center instead?

Then the Residence Inn becomes more attractive. You would save roughly $30-$70 all-in, get breakfast on Friday, and have a room setup that is clearer on fridge and coffee. The only loss is being outside the event hub.
What about getting from MSP to downtown without a car?

Blue Line light rail is the simplest no-car option if you are arriving midafternoon: roughly 25-30 minutes to downtown for a few dollars, then a short walk or quick rideshare depending on the hotel. A rideshare is easier with luggage or rain, usually about 20-30 minutes and often $32-$45. For Friday, I would budget a rideshare to MSP if you take the 2:45 return.
For Wednesday dinner, would the event hotel be less of a hassle?

Yes. The Hilton gives you an on-site fallback and several nearby downtown options after the reception. The Depot area also has good Mill District choices, but you may end up traveling back from the reception anyway, so its dinner advantage is smaller on Wednesday.
What would you do before the block cutoff?

Ask the organizer one question: where is the first 8:00-9:00 Thursday item? If it is at the Hilton, hold the refundable block room before the cutoff. If Thursday starts later or elsewhere, take the Residence Inn refundable room and keep the United ORD nonstop option with the Friday 2:45 return.
Anything I should verify in the hotel language?

For either hotel, verify the all-in total, cancellation deadline, whether breakfast is included or covered only by the meeting, in-room coffee maker, refrigerator or mini-fridge, Wi-Fi, and Friday bag storage after checkout. For the Hilton block, specifically confirm the block room type and whether a fridge is standard or must be requested.

messages.content: Minneapolis update: the organizer confirmed Thursday starts with an 8:00 breakfast briefing inside the Hilton. Block cutoff is Friday. The Residence Inn at The Depot is still $179 refundable with breakfast. Can you compare the two after tax and the local rideshares?

Yes. I will use April 22-24, two nights, about 15% lodging tax, United ORD-MSP at about $306, no rental car, and similar airport transfers for both. Is the Hilton still $219 and cancellable 72 hours out?
Yes, $219 block, cancellation 72 hours before arrival. No breakfast listed except the Thursday meeting breakfast. Residence Inn cancellation says by April 20.

Side-by-side: Hotel | Lodging after tax | Extra local transport | Thursday morning | Breakfast/room basics | Est. trip total. Hilton block | about $504 | $0 for meeting moves; same airport transfer as either hotel | elevator or short walk downstairs for 8:00 | Thursday meeting breakfast; room coffee likely, mini-fridge needs block confirmation | about $840-$850. Residence Inn at The Depot | about $412 | plan $35-$55 for Wed reception, Thu morning, and possible return rideshares | leave around 7:20-7:25 for the 8:00 briefing | breakfast included, coffee + fridge/kitchen setup clearer | about $810-$825. Net savings is probably only $25-$40 if you use rideshares.
So the breakfast included at Residence Inn is not as valuable because Thursday breakfast is part of the meeting.
Exactly. It helps Friday morning and maybe with snacks, but it does not offset much of the early-Thursday friction.
Could I just walk from the Depot Thursday morning?

Possible, but I would not build the plan around it for an 8:00 start with work clothes and weather uncertainty. It is roughly a 15-18 minute walk depending on the entrance; a rideshare keeps the margin cleaner.
What about Wednesday dinner if I reserve the Hilton?

Hilton is easier: there is an on-site restaurant/bar and plenty of downtown options close by after the reception. At the Depot, dinner choices are good in the Mill District, but you would still be commuting back after the reception.
Do we know the room has a coffee maker and mini-fridge?

For Hilton, the coffee maker is commonly listed, but the fridge language can vary by room or block. I would add a request and call or message the hotel to confirm. Residence Inn is stronger on that point because the room setup usually includes a fridge or kitchen area.
Okay, I’m going to reserve the Hilton. Last booking notes?

Reserve the refundable Hilton block before Friday. The likely premium is small after rideshares, and it removes the only fussy morning of the trip. Put notes to confirm a non-smoking room in the room type you choose, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, Wi-Fi, Friday bag storage, and the exact cancellation deadline. Keep the United after-lunch return as planned unless Friday’s wrap-up gets extended.
